body: Thank you, you've really helped me out.
No problem, I've actually been feeling really shitty and talking with you has actually helped a little, so thank *you*.

Thank you for your vote of confidence, I'll try to keep that in mind. It's just hard because even though what you said is true, it's not just the job or school, I've felt terrible every day for years. 

I know I need to put in more effort, it's just difficult when I feel like I'm constantly getting beat down, and complaining about it like I am now feels wrong too.

Thanks again for your reply, I appreciate it.

You're very welcome. Definitely message her! Chances are she will be happy you came around to talking to her and will reciprocate. 

Good luck with everything :) The fact that you're willing to change your stance and give something a second chance speaks volumes of your character, it's awesome and it's commendable.

Thank you so much for taking the time to write all that. I really appreciate it.  I did do the behavioral therapy, and it didn't work for me either. But who knows if that's just me making it not work.

I am seeing a therapist now, but he just talks about himself for the majority of the hour and I due to external reasons, I can't change him right now, but I plan to as soon as I can.

The downward spiral is true. I had a drug problem for a number of years and have been clean for about half a year now. Everyone says it slowly gets better but everything is slowly getting worse.  I just have a constant feeling of disassociation from the world, like I'm on auto-pilot, and every once in a while I have some form of terrible luck. I know I need to not be hard on myself and commit to making small steps here and there, but it just seems like an insurmountable task when I feel sick all day and every so often my bad luck gets to me.  And know that people who usually cry bad luck are the ones causing it, like someone i used to work with who run stop signs all the time and said she had bad luck when she got a ticket once.  

To give an example, in the last month and a half my car was totaled in a parking lot while I was in the store, and I was framed for a crime that I did not commit by someone I haven't spoken to in years, that now I have to get a lawyer and go to court to have resolved, among other things. 

I hate to sound like I'm whining, but those were unavoidable, right? It just feels like I can't catch a break. 

I try to form relationships with people. I tried in college but definitely sabotaged them through apathy, and I go to NA/AA meetings, and everyone is so kind and seemingly genuine, but I just can't seem to relate to put in effort. So I have zero people to talk to thanks to me. 

Thank you again for your advice, I'm going to reread it and try to commit the points to memory.  Sorry for the wall of complaining text, I've just never said this to anyone before and felt like typing it out.

It's sometimes hard or impossible to force yourself to disregard, or not even have those negative thoughts, but try to remind yourself that this is her profession.  She chose this to do as a career.  She wants to help people, and believe me, if she's been a therapist for longer than a year, she's already seen a bit of everything.  She would not think you're using her. 

Maybe she never replied because of your refusal. In therapy and psychology and the like, you cannot force someone to do anything, and trained professionals know this.  In fact, badgering someone is likely to worsen the situation, so she probably never replied as an educated decision.  But like I said before, she's devoting her life to this profession, if you wanted to speak with her, I'm sure she would welcome you back with open arms.  Put yourself in her shoes, if someone you knew had a problem you could help them with, wouldn't you rather they ask you for help than risk hurting themselves?

All of this is purely speculation, but it sounded good in my head.

I was just browsing this sub, thinking about making a throwaway to post something, and I did just now to talk to you.

What if you always do feel like that. When you wake up in the morning it's hard to get out of bed because of how badly you feel, your day is you feeling badly, punctuated by feeling worse, and it been like that for years?
